data.name: Aayan
data.gender_notes: Aayan is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who preserves or guards something, often used for names of protectors or caretakers. The name Aayan carries the meaning “Preserver, Guardian” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Aayan usually hope their child will grow to embody preserver, guardian and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A reminder of Allah's guidance and protection throughout one's life journey.
data.etymology: Aayan belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Preserver, Guardian.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Aayan total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

in_arabic.name: أَیّان
in_arabic.long_meaning: أَیّان هو اسم مُستعار من كلمة الأَیّام، والذي يُشير إلى الوقت الحاضر والمُستقبَل، والذي يُعتبر مُقدسًا في الإسلام حيث يُمثل العُمر الحَقيقي والجَميل الذي يتمتع به المُؤمن، وقد يُستخدم هذا الاسم كي يُرمز إلى الحَياة الحاضرة والمُستقبلة التي يتمتع بها الإنسان، والذى يُعتبر مُجملًا ومُستمرًا ومُستقبِلًا.

in_english.meaning: time, present, future, current age, age of innocence, blissful life

This name can be used to symbolize the present and future life that man enjoys, which is a whole and continuous and future life.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Aayan" is of Arabic origin and is often used among Muslim communities. In many cultures, there is a deep appreciation and emphasis on the role of protectors and guardians, reflecting the communal values that prioritize preserving and safeguarding the welfare of families and communities. The name "Aayan" represents the idea of an individual being responsible for the preservation and security of something valuable, and this cultural significance can manifest spiritually in several ways.
data.spiritual_significance: In the Islamic tradition, the name "Aayan" holds a deep spiritual significance, reminding the bearer of the responsibility they have towards protecting and preserving their faith, morals, and values. This spiritual role can extend beyond the individual's immediate self and circle and encompass their community and even larger societal context. The name calls upon its bearer to be steadfast, vigilant, and committed in their spiritual journey, always striving to protect and uphold the divine guidance as entrusted to them.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The meaning "Preserver, Guardian" symbolizes One who preserves or guards something, often used for names of protectors or caretakers..
